author: Michael Larabel
description: Adding to all the exciting performance optimizations and other improvements for Linux 7.4 is an exciting workqueue improvement. It's not too often getting to talk about "10 to 100 times faster" software improvements...
title: Linux 7.4 Workqueue Changes Bring A "10 To 100 Times Faster" Optimization

author: Michael Larabel
description: Fedora 45 wasn't released this week as its ideal early release target due to not having a release candidate build in time for last week's Go/No-Go meeting. At today's Go/No-Go meeting, Fedora 45 was delayed by at least one more week due to open blocker bugs...
title: Fedora 45 Hits A Second NO-GO: Not Releasing Until November

author: Michael Larabel
description: A request for comments (RFC) was sent out last night on the Linux kernel mailing list in seeking to clean-up the AMD Zen microarchitecture detection within the kernel. This is for enhancing the kernel where there are code paths specific to a certain generation of AMD Zen processors or select generations such as Zen 3 through Zen 5 CPUs. AI was leveraged in helping to clean-up this AMD Zen code in the Linux kernel...
title: AI Helping To Improve Linux's AMD Zen CPU Microarchitecture Detection

author: Michael Larabel
description: Back in August Modular's Mojo language was open-sourced following the acquisition of Chris Lattner's company by Qualcomm. The latest achievement now out of the company is their MAX software being fully opened up with the entire source tree available...
title: Modular's MAX Source Code Now Fully Opened, Under New MAX License

author: Michael Larabel
description: The scheduler updates have been merged for the in-development Linux 7.4 kernel to deliver several nice scheduling enhancements...
title: Linux 7.4 Improves Scheduling Latency For Short-Slice Tasks, NVIDIA Vera SMT Preference

author: Michael Larabel
description: Linux user-space for several years had shadow stack support for hardware-enforced control-flow enforcement in defending against return oriented programming (ROP) attacks. Intel Tigerlake and newer CPUs or AMD Zen 3 and newer have the necessary hardware shadow stacks support. Shadow stacks have been effective for helping user-space software fend ROP attacks while now there is new work toward bringing shadow stack support for kernel space on Linux...
title: x86 Kernel Shadow Stacks Being Worked On For Linux As Powerful Control Flow Protection

author: Michael Larabel
description: The Mesa 3D graphics driver project has loosened its rules laid out in their AGENTS.md for AI agents to permit AI/LLM assistance in generating code comments and commit/patch messages, as long as a human is ultimately reviewing/editing it in the end...
title: Mesa Loosens Rules Around AI Agents For Code Comments / Commit Messages

author: Michael Larabel
description: Myrlyn, the package manager GUI that began as YQPkg during a SUSE Hack Week and has evolved quite well, is out with version 1.1 as the first new feature update since the beginning of the year...
title: Myrlyn 1.1 Released For SUSE/openSUSE GUI Package Manager

author: Michael Larabel
description: Valve landed a patch in Mesa 27.0 and to be back-ported to current Mesa stable series to satisfy more games running under Steam Play with VKD3D-Proton for working on AMD GFX8 GPUs like Polaris...
title: Mesa RADV Change Satisfies More Steam Play Games On Aging AMD GFX8 GPUs

author: Michael Larabel
description: The x86/bugs pull request was merged this week for the Linux 7.4 kernel. Most notable here is adjusting the CPU security mitigations for AMD Zen 6 processors...
title: Linux 7.4 Adapts AMD Zen 6 For Less Costly CPU Security Mitigation
